preamble: Lowering and fronting the open-mid back unrounded [ʌ] gives open [a]. In Korean the Middle Korean vowel ㆍ (arae-a, usually reconstructed as /ʌ/) merged with a in word-initial syllables, and with ɨ elsewhere; only Jeju keeps a distinct reflex. In London English the STRUT vowel, [ʌ] in RP, is fronted and lowered to [ɐ̟] or cardinal [a] in Cockney.

examples.note: In non-initial syllables ㆍ merged instead with ㅡ ɨ, e.g. 하ᄂᆞᆶ hànólh > 하늘 haneul 'sky'.
The first-syllable ㆍ became a and the second became ɨ.
Cockney /a/ corresponds to RP /ʌ/ and is realized as [ɐ̟] or cardinal [a]. A similar open front [a] is reported for STRUT in border areas of north and mid Wales.

sources: Lee, K.-M., & Ramsey, S. R. (2011). A History of the Korean Language. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511974045
Wells, J. C. (1982). Accents of English. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511611759
